events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to South Haven by boat.** I'd rate it **3 (good)** for this week, the best of the four.
- **Grand Haven 2 (average) and Muskegon 2 (average).** Both are workable if South Haven is out of reach.
- **St. Joseph 1 (below average).** Skip it for boats this week.
- **Run lines at about 40 to 90 feet down** in 60 to 120 feet of water, using glow spoons, rotators, and green or white flies.

## Why
- South Haven is the only port whose latest boat report was rated good, and that report found fish in 110 to 120 feet of water (South Haven, 2022-09-07).
- Grand Haven and Muskegon both had average boat reports that week, with the best action 40 to 90 feet down (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-09-07).
- St. Joseph's only boat report was rated below average, with spoons catching most of the fish (St. Joseph, 2022-09-07).
- I'd expect fish to sit deeper than the 73 F surface, since the reports put them 40 to 90 feet down, and that is where cooler water is likely.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is 2022-09-07, six days old)
- South Haven, boat, quality 3: "Salmon anglers reported pretty good fishing this week." Fish were in 110 to 120 feet, with "some good fish caught deeper also," and the best water was "around 40 feet." Lures were spoons, rotators, and flies.
- Grand Haven, boat, quality 2: "The salmon action was fair." Water was 40 to 120 feet, fish 40 to 85 feet down, on glow spoons and green or white flies. The pier was "slow for salmon."
- Muskegon, boat, quality 2: "The salmon action was fair." Water was 60 to 120 feet, fish 45 to 90 feet down, on glow plugs, orange or green spoons, and green flies. No salmon were reported from the breakwalls.
- St. Joseph, boat, quality 1: "Salmon anglers were catching fish when they could get on the lake." The best water was about 100 feet, and spoons caught most fish.
- Earlier in August the boat reports were mostly average or below, with scattered fish (Grand Haven 2022-08-24 and 2022-08-17; Muskegon 2022-08-17; South Haven 2022-08-24).

**Past seasons**
- A search for earlier seasons with surface water near 72 F found only the same September 7 reports. I found no earlier-season matches, so I have no historical pattern to add.

**Conditions now**
- Live data was unavailable, so these are the buoy readings for the week before today: surface water averaged 72 to 73 F at all four ports, down 1 to 3 F over the week (St. Joseph 73 F, -3 F; South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon about 72 F, -1 F).
- There is no modeled cold-layer depth and no wind forecast in this data, so I can't say whether there is upwelling or what the wind will do.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F, so at 72 F surface water the fish are probably holding deeper.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and fall conditions can shift quickly. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- The conditions data is a buoy summary, not live. Check the current wind forecast before heading out; if it's strong, the pier or river may be the safer choice.
- The buoys are miles offshore, so the surface figures don't describe conditions at each pier.

## Sources
- Michigan DNR weekly report, Sept 7 (all four ports): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- Michigan DNR weekly report, Aug 24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
- Michigan DNR weekly report, Aug 17: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
